housing: Wigan borough is made up of several former mining and mill towns, including Wigan, Leigh, Atherton, Tyldesley and Ashton-in-Makerfield. Red-brick Victorian terraces are common, alongside large post-war council estates and many new estates built on former colliery and industrial land. Prices are among the lowest in Greater Manchester, and private renting rose quickly between 2011 and 2021 though it stays below the national level. Much of the private rented stock is older terraces and ex-council houses.
checkinTips: Victorian terraces: photograph back yards, outhouses, damp in rear kitchens and the condition of back alleys and gates.
Older homes in former mining areas: note any cracks in walls, sticking doors or uneven floors that could point to movement.
Ex-council houses and maisonettes: record communal areas, bin stores, fences and any garages in blocks.
New-build estates in Standish, Leigh and Golborne: check sealant, flooring and snagging marks, and who maintains shared land.
Flats over shops in town centres: note separate entrances, meter cupboards and rear fire escapes.
Homes near the canal and flashes: photograph any damp, gutters and gardens prone to waterlogging.
tenantHelp: Wigan Council's private sector housing and HMO team investigates disrepair and unsafe conditions in private rented homes.
